about: What a `<data>` element's XML content and an XML `_event.data` answer when
a document reads them, written out by hand against DOM Level 1 Core.
W3C SCXML B.2.1 obliges the Processor to create "the corresponding DOM
structure" for XML content, and B.2.8.1 says the same for an arriving
payload. That is an interface, not a pair of method names — and a pair of
method names is what every SCE backend supplied. Measured 2026-08-18, all
seven carried `getElementsByTagName`, `getAttribute` and a non-standard
`getTagName`, which are exactly the two names the W3C IRP suite reads plus
one, so `d.tagName`, `d.childNodes` and `d.firstChild` reached every engine
as a nil index while 204/204 W3C fixtures passed.
Every reader of this file is measured against it: the two C++ engines
(tests/engine/DomReadSurfaceTest.cpp), the three Kotlin engines, the Rust,
Go and Python bindings, and the frontend that lowers the expressions
(sce-build/tests/dom_read_surface_table.rs). A per-backend copy of a table
drifts toward the backend that reads it; one table cannot.
Two spellings per case, because the readers divide by what they are handed.
`source` is the author's ECMAScript, which the engines that run ECMAScript
evaluate as written — the Kotlin Rhino and QuickJS engines, and both C++
engines (the C++ Lua engine rewrites it itself). `lua` is the same
expression after the frontend has lowered it, which is all the Rust, Go,
Python and Kotlin-Lua backends ever see, because their translation happens
at build time. The pair is not a guess: `dom_read_surface_table.rs` asserts
that the frontend's own lowering of `source` IS `lua`, so a case cannot
claim a lowering the emitter does not produce.
The tree is the cpp reference backend's, which parses with pugixml's
`parse_default`. That flag set omits `parse_ws_pcdata`, `parse_comments`
and `parse_pi`, so a whitespace-only text run, a comment and a processing
instruction are not nodes — which is why `books` is pretty-printed and its
document element has exactly two children.

cases.group: whitespace that is not the only thing in its run
cases.note: The rule pugixml's parse_default applies is `whitespace-ONLY runs are not nodes`, and the two halves of that are easy to conflate: a run of `a ` keeps its trailing space and a run of ` c` keeps its leading one. Measured 2026-08-18, three of the seven bindings skipped whitespace before deciding whether text followed, so ` c` reached the datamodel as `c` — invisible while nothing could read text at all.
